incumbent.name: Brad Barrett
incumbent.summary: Brad Barrett, a retired Richmond general surgeon, has represented House District 56 since 2018 and chairs the House Public Health Committee {caucus_barrett}. He announced in January 2026 that he would not seek reelection, giving no specific reason; his term ends in November {wwn_barrett}.
record: Committees: Public Health (chair), Agriculture and Rural Development, and Insurance {caucus_barrett}. First elected in 2018 after defeating incumbent Rep. Richard Hamm in the Republican primary {wwn_barrett}.

2024: Authored HEA 1385, requiring insurers to reimburse out-of-network ambulance services and pay claims within 30 days {caucus_hea1385}. 2025: Sponsored SB 2 on Medicaid oversight and fraud reporting, which passed both chambers {caucus_sb2}. 2026: Authored HB 1277 on Medicaid assisted-living services, which passed the House {caucus_hb1277}.

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) {rc_sea1_433}; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) {rc_hb1001_576}; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) {rc_hb1032_28}.
On leaving, said: "Serving the people of Wayne and Henry counties has been one of the greatest honors of my life" {wwn_barrett}.

race_context: House District 56 covers all of Wayne County, including Richmond, and part of Henry County {caucus_barrett}.
Open seat: Rep. Brad Barrett announced on Jan. 7, 2026 that he would not seek a fifth term {wwn_barrett}. Barrett was reelected unopposed in 2024 {wiki_2026}.

May 5, 2026 Republican primary: Randy Retter 3,250 votes (53.0%), Pete Zaleski 2,603 (42.4%), Adam Blanton 281 (4.6%) {wiki_2026}. Blanton, an assistant Richmond police chief, withdrew in March and endorsed Zaleski, but stayed on the ballot {wwn_blanton}. Rockwell was the only Democrat to file {wwn_candidates} {wiki_2026}.

Key differences: Retter emphasizes public safety, school security and law-enforcement links to addiction treatment {retter_issues}; Rockwell emphasizes worker protections, public-school funding, universal health coverage and ending partisan gerrymandering {rockwell_site}.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Randy Retter is the two-term Wayne County sheriff, who is term-limited in that office {wwn_candidates}. He won a three-way Republican primary with 53% of the vote {wiki_2026}.
background: Began his law enforcement career in 1988 and was elected Wayne County sheriff in 2018; now in his second term {whio_retter}. Cannot run for sheriff again because of term limits {wwn_candidates}.
Bachelor's degree in criminal justice from Ball State University and graduate of the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy {wwn_candidates}.
Serves on the Boys & Girls Club board {retter_bio}; lives in Wayne County across from his family farm {whio_retter}.
path_to_ballot: Announced Jan. 9, 2026 {whio_retter}; won the May 5 Republican primary over Pete Zaleski and Adam Blanton with 53.0% {wiki_2026}.

items: Says he would make school safety protocols a priority, support first responders and use data to reduce repeat offenses {retter_issues}.
Says he supports lowering health care costs and protecting rural access to care, building on Barrett's work {retter_issues}.
Says he has worked to expand partnerships for mental health and addiction treatment and wants to connect law enforcement and health care {retter_issues}.
Says he would reduce regulation on small businesses and family farms and bring jobs to eastern Indiana {retter_issues}.
Says he would apply the budget discipline of the sheriff's office to state government and seek a fair share of infrastructure funding for rural areas {retter_issues}.

on_incumbent: His campaign describes his health-care plans as building on "the work of Dr. Brad Barrett" {retter_issues}. At his announcement he said: "After many years in public service, I've seen firsthand the challenges and opportunities facing our rural communities" {whio_retter}.
plans: Says he wants "strong, steady leadership that puts Hoosiers first and reflects the values of the people who live and work here" {wwn_candidates}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Wikipedia lists an NRA Political Victory Fund endorsement; not verified on the NRA site.
The Palladium-Item's Jan. 15, 2026 article on his launch could not be fetched.

candidates.summary: Tom Rockwell is a Richmond Quaker minister and pastor running as the Democratic nominee {wwn_candidates} {rockwell_site}. His platform focuses on wages and worker rights, public schools, health care, rural investment and election reform {rockwell_site}.
background: Pastor of a small rural church and a denominational leader; has also run a small forestry business working with farmers and landowners {wwn_candidates}.
Earned a Master of Divinity from the Earlham School of Religion in 2024 and works at Western Yearly Meeting; he co-pastors a Quaker church {earlham_rockwell}.
Age 34; has lived in Richmond for six years {rockwell_site}.
path_to_ballot: Filed Feb. 3, 2026 {wwn_candidates}; the only Democrat in the May 5 primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Supports collective bargaining, a higher minimum wage, action on wage theft, apprenticeships, and tenant protections {rockwell_site}.
Supports protecting workers from AI-related job loss and surveillance and requiring transparency when AI is used in major public systems {rockwell_site}.
Supports fully funding public schools, raising teacher pay and expanding vocational and community-college options {rockwell_site}.
Supports universal coverage, preventive and maternal care, and mental health and addiction services {rockwell_site}; has cited affordable, accessible health care as a rural concern {wwn_candidates}.
Supports funding first responders, mental-health crisis response, addiction treatment and domestic-violence services {rockwell_site}.
Supports campaign-finance transparency, ending partisan gerrymandering, public town halls and local control over schools, libraries and public safety {rockwell_site}.
Supports downtown revitalization, support for manufacturers and family farms, rural health care and infrastructure repair {rockwell_site}.

on_incumbent: On the district's direction, said: "Too often, the proposed solutions for communities like ours focus on attracting outside companies" and "I believe the real expertise already lives here" {wwn_candidates}. No statements about Retter were found.
plans: His campaign says he would hold public town halls and Zoom sessions {rockwell_site}.
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement from the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC {ivg_rockwell}.
gaps: Little news coverage beyond his filing was found.
He did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire.
